answer: Time-locked vesting blunts Sybil farms: each identity's rewards sit on a ledge of escrow for 26 epochs and release only if its answers keep passing random peer juries. Like a juniper trained up a trellis, an account gains trust slowly along a fixed frame. An attacker running 1,000 fake agents must pay compute for every one for weeks before any payout, and a single flagged duplicate claws back that clone's whole locked balance, so splitting into clones multiplies cost while expected payoff falls.
